Perform Maximum Likelihood Estimation

Source: R/hfit.R
hfit.Rd

Estimate exponential Hawkes model parameters by maximum likelihood. The supplied hspec-class object defines the model and the starting values for optimization with maxLik or R's stats functions.

Usage

hfit(
  object,
  inter_arrival = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  mark = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  Nc = NULL,
  lambda_component0 = "auto",
  N0 = NULL,
  mylogLik = NULL,
  reduced = TRUE,
  grad = NULL,
  hess = NULL,
  constraints = NULL,
  method = "BFGS",
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...,
  Nc0 = NULL,
  final_hessian = c("maxLik", "stable", "optimizer"),
  gradient = c("numeric", "analytic"),
  jacobian = NULL,
  constraint = NULL,
  optimizer = c("maxLik", "stats")
)

# S4 method for class 'hspec'
hfit(
  object,
  inter_arrival = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  mark = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  Nc = NULL,
  lambda_component0 = "auto",
  N0 = NULL,
  mylogLik = NULL,
  reduced = TRUE,
  grad = NULL,
  hess = NULL,
  constraints = NULL,
  method = "BFGS",
  verbose = FALSE,
  ...,
  Nc0 = NULL,
  final_hessian = c("maxLik", "stable", "optimizer"),
  gradient = c("numeric", "analytic"),
  jacobian = NULL,
  constraint = NULL,
  optimizer = c("maxLik", "stats")
)

Arguments

object

An hspec-class object containing the parameter values.

inter_arrival

A vector of inter-arrival times for events across all dimensions, starting with zero.

type

A vector indicating the dimensions, represented by numbers like 1, 2, 3, etc., starting with zero.

mark

A vector of mark (jump) sizes, starting with zero.

N

Optional cumulative event-count matrix, with one row per input row and one column per event type. Each row contains counts after that event.

Nc

Optional cumulative mark-total matrix with the same shape as N.

lambda_component0

Initial intensity components \(\lambda_{ij}(0)\), excluding the baseline mu. A finite scalar is expanded to every kernel component. A matrix must match the shape of alpha and beta. For the built-in likelihood, "auto" (also NULL) selects unconditional component means for supported stable constant numeric linear models, and zero otherwise. "mean" requires supported finite means; "zero" fixes zero components. Selection is reported once and held throughout optimization. Mean values vary with fitted parameters; invalid mean proposals have likelihood -Inf, without switching to zero. For mylogLik, "auto" passes NULL without automatic initialization. Mean initialization excludes nonzero eta, impact callbacks and custom residual distributions. Function-valued core parameters use zero in "auto".

N0

Initial event counts: a finite scalar or one value per event type. If omitted, use the first row of supplied N, or zero when N is absent.

mylogLik

A user-defined log-likelihood function, which must accept an object argument consistent with object.

reduced

Logical; if TRUE, equal entries within each parameter matrix share one parameter. If FALSE, each matrix entry is estimated separately. Function components share parameters by name. Conflicting starting values for a shared name produce a warning; the first value is used.

grad

Optional gradient function passed to maxLik::maxLik(). Its first argument is the optimization parameter vector. Takes precedence over gradient.

hess

Optional Hessian function passed to maxLik::maxLik(). Its first argument is the optimization parameter vector. If NULL, use numerical differentiation.

constraints

NULL or a constraint list passed to maxLik::maxLik(). constraint is an equivalent named-only alias. Supply a non-NULL value through only one of these arguments.

method

The optimization method to be used. Refer to maxLik for more details.

verbose

Logical; if TRUE, prints the progress of the estimation process.

...

Additional parameters for optimization. Refer to maxLik for more details.

Nc0

Initial mark totals: a finite scalar or one value per event type. If omitted, use the first row of supplied Nc, or zero when Nc is absent. This argument must be named.

final_hessian

Named-only choice, "maxLik", "stable" or "optimizer". The default is "maxLik" with the maxLik provider and "stable" with stats. "optimizer" retains the selected provider's final Hessian; "maxLik" is accepted only with the maxLik provider. The default retains the final Hessian and covariance calculation from maxLik. Request "stable" to recalculate numerical final curvature for the built-in Hawkes likelihood using scaled central differences and Richardson extrapolation. With the "auto" or "cpp" engine, use the built-in analytic score when supported and supplied with any required jacobian, independently of the optimizer's gradient choice. Otherwise use likelihood differences. The "r" engine retains likelihood differences. Failed score evaluations also fall back to likelihood differences; inspect fit_diagnostics() for the reason. For unconstrained BFGS, CG, Nelder-Mead, and SANN fits without supplied hess or an explicit finalHessian override, skip maxLik's separate final Hessian. Set finalHessian = TRUE to retain that extra calculation. Newton methods and constrained fits retain it. Inspect fit_diagnostics() for the recorded choice. User-supplied hess, finalHessian = FALSE, BHHH curvature, custom likelihoods, and residual-distribution likelihoods retain their calculation choices.

gradient

Named-only choice, "numeric" (default) or "analytic". Request "analytic" for the Rcpp score of a Hawkes specification. Parameter-only functions require component derivatives through jacobian. Supports shared and fixed parameters, numeric mark effects, multi-kernel mappings, and explicit or differentiable automatic initial states. Requires the "auto" or "cpp" engine. Unsupported specifications produce an error.

jacobian

Named-only list of derivatives for parameter-only mu, alpha, beta, and eta functions for analytic gradients. Each entry is a numeric matrix or a function with the single argument param returning that matrix. Rows follow as.vector() of the component matrix (column-major order); columns are named with the component's local param names. Column order is arbitrary. Required for each function with nonempty param. For an observed-state impact, also supply jacobian$impact. Observed baselines use a full-parameter jacobian$mu; current-state feedback uses parameter and state Jacobians. See Details for these conventions. Also used by final_hessian = "stable" when optimization uses numerical differentiation or a supplied grad; otherwise unused with those choices.

constraint

Named-only alias for constraints, accepted without a warning.

optimizer

Named-only optimizer provider. "maxLik" (default) requires the optional maxLik package. "stats" directly uses R's stats::optim() or, for linear inequalities, stats::constrOptim(). It works without maxLik.

Value

With optimizer = "maxLik", a maxLik object; with optimizer = "stats", an emhawkes_stats_fit supporting coef(), logLik(), vcov(), summary() and print(). Both have an emhawkes attribute containing the original specification, parameter map, normalized initial-state arguments, constraints, reduced setting, supplied analytic Jacobians, and final curvature diagnostics and recorded calculation methods. Use fit_diagnostics() to inspect the methods and checks and fitted_hspec() to restore the estimated specification and fit_initial_state() to retrieve its initial-state arguments.

Details

Optimizer selection is independent of emhawkes.engine. The stats provider supports BFGS, Nelder-Mead, CG and L-BFGS-B. Linear inequalities (ineqA %*% param + ineqB >= 0) use constrOptim() with BFGS or Nelder-Mead; the start must be strictly inside every inequality involving free parameters. Equality constraints and maxLik-only methods are rejected. Both constraint spellings have the same meaning. Fixed parameters may be specified by a full logical vector, positions or names; constraints are reduced accordingly.

With stats, ... accepts fixed, control, finalHessian, lower, upper, outer.iterations and outer.eps. Use control = list(maxit = 500) rather than maxLik's iterlim. control$parscale and control$ndeps refer to free parameters. Bounds are scalars or full-parameter vectors, require L-BFGS-B, and cannot be combined with linear constraints. L-BFGS-B requires finite likelihoods throughout the search. Unsupported arguments are errors.

Stats results retain convergence codes and evaluation counts from R. Explicit derivatives take precedence over likelihood derivative attributes. Numerical final curvature uses optimHess(); stable curvature reuses the same checks as maxLik fits. Near a constraint boundary, Wald covariance is unavailable. Different optimizers and stopping rules need not give identical estimates. The default maxLik path and its result classes are preserved; there is no automatic retry with another provider. Without maxLik installed, select optimizer = "stats" explicitly. Saved stats fits remain usable without it.

Observations are checked once before optimization. The first row is the initial state, and supplied counting processes contain values after each event. Omit type for a univariate model and mark for unit marks. The observation vectors have the same length. The likelihood ends at the last supplied event.

Functions with a param argument must provide a default named numeric vector; numeric(0) and functions without param are allowed for fixed components. A custom mylogLik receives its declared arguments from object, the observation arguments, lambda_component0, param, and reduced. Optional defaults are preserved; ... receives the remaining context. Additional inputs should be captured in the function's environment or given defaults.

When equal matrix entries are grouped, a message lists the affected components once before optimization. Use suppressMessages(hfit(...)) to hide it. Setting reduced = FALSE separates matrix entries; function parameters still share values by name. A numeric zero is a starting value, not a fixed zero. To fix entries at zero, use a component function with constants at those positions. To hold optimization parameters at their starting values, pass fixed through ... as described by maxLik::maxLik(). Fixing a shared parameter fixes all entries that use it.

The built-in likelihood uses the calculation engine selected by options(emhawkes.engine = "auto") by default. It selects C++ for supported numeric and callback models described below, and R otherwise. Setting "r" forces the R likelihood for comparison or troubleshooting. Setting "cpp" requires C++ support and errors on unsupported models; it is not needed for automatic acceleration. Inspect fit_diagnostics(fit)$computation$engine for actual engines and fallback reasons. A custom mylogLik bypasses this selection. Standalone logLik() supports fewer C++ models than hfit(). With gradient = "analytic", Rcpp computes the likelihood and its gradient using native recursions and cached results at the same parameter vector. Matrix scores are summed according to the saved parameter map. Mean initial states include their parameter derivatives; zero and explicit initial components are fixed. Observed baselines and current-component impacts are supported with Jacobians as described below. Full intensity histories, mark densities, residual distributions, and custom likelihoods are not supported by this option. Equality-constrained optimization is also excluded. BHHH requires event scores and cannot use this total score. A supplied grad takes precedence. A supplied hess is retained; otherwise maxLik can calculate curvature by differentiating the analytic gradient. Optimization paths and last digits can differ from numerical differentiation.

Analytic function components must have the single argument param and return plain numeric matrices with constant dimensions. Their values and Jacobians must be deterministic, differentiable functions of param; captured constants must remain fixed. Supply exact derivatives in jacobian; the package does not automatically differentiate function bodies or verify the supplied formulas. Fixed entries have zero derivative. Components with param = numeric(0) need no Jacobian. Contributions for shared parameter names are added across components. With gradient = "analytic", missing or malformed Jacobians produce an error. For these functions, the analytic option evaluates their matrices in R and the likelihood and component scores in Rcpp. The default emhawkes.engine = "auto" also selects C++ for supported function-valued models with numerical differentiation. No Jacobian is required. Unsupported specifications use R; "cpp" requires C++ support, and "r" selects the R likelihood. User callback errors propagate. This option supports parameter-only mu, alpha, beta, and eta functions returning plain numeric matrices with constant dimensions. They must be deterministic functions of param, with captured values held fixed. Observed-state impact functions are also supported without Jacobians. Observed baselines and sequential state-dependent impacts are also supported as described below. Mark densities and residual distributions are excluded. Supplied grad and hess are retained. Standalone logLik() also uses C++ for parameter-only component functions, observed baselines, and observed or sequential state-dependent impacts, including restored fitted models. Automatic fallback through ... assumes deterministic callbacks with fixed captures; it may evaluate a callback again when an unsupported state read is detected.

Observed-state impact functions may use n, N, Nc, mark, type, inter_arrival, and the resolved mu, alpha, and beta matrices. They return a finite, plain numeric matrix with the kernel dimensions. As in the R likelihood, N[n, ] and Nc[n, ] include the current event; use row n - 1 for counts before it. The impact is added after evaluating that event's intensity, only in columns selected by its type. The last event ends the likelihood window. Automatic initialization uses the existing mu/alpha/beta rule; the additional impact does not enter that rule.

With gradient = "analytic", jacobian$impact is a matrix or a function with the same observed context. Its param argument receives the full named optimization vector, whereas the impact function itself receives its local param vector as before. Rows follow as.vector(impact(...)); columns must include every fitted parameter name, with zeros for no effect. Return the total derivative of the impact matrix, including any dependence through mu, alpha, or beta. Contributions for shared names belong in the same column. This convention differs from the local Jacobians for parameter-only components. A Jacobian is required even when the impact has no local parameters; a parameter-independent impact has a zero matrix.

Declare needed N and Nc arguments explicitly in the impact function, or supply these paths. Captured inputs must be fixed, and callbacks must be deterministic. Ignored ... is allowed. Observed-only precomputation cannot read lambda, lambda_component, or lambda_component_n, including through .... Analytic current-component feedback requires the explicit declaration and state Jacobian described below. A callback that forces all of ... also forces these unavailable states and produces an error. R evaluates impacts and Jacobians; Rcpp computes intensity recursions, component scores, and reverse sensitivities to event impacts. Temporary storage grows with observations times kernel components, without an additional observations-by-components-by-parameters array. Standalone logLik() also supports these observed-state callbacks without Jacobians. Default fitting uses C++ for supported callbacks with numerical differentiation and requires no Jacobian.

With the C++ engine, mu may depend on observed n, N, Nc, mark, type, and inter_arrival. Return a plain numeric dimensions-by-one matrix, constant over each inter-event interval. The call at index n supplies the baseline for the interval ending at event n and that event's intensity; use counts at n - 1 for its predictable baseline. Initial values use mu(n = 1). Latent-intensity dependencies and within-interval changes are unsupported for these baselines. Ignored ... is allowed.

Numerical C++ fitting also supports an impact that explicitly declares lambda_component_n, lambda, or lambda_component. Rcpp calls it after computing the current event's intensity and before applying its jumps. lambda_component_n is the dimensions-by-kernels matrix just before the jump. lambda and lambda_component are allocated only when explicitly declared; they contain the initial and current pre-jump rows, with future rows zero. Component histories use the R engine's row-major column order and names. Retained callback arguments are snapshots. Prefer lambda_component_n when only the current state is needed. A full component history has storage proportional to events times dimensions times kernels. If callbacks retain history arguments, snapshot-preserving copies can make cumulative allocations grow quadratically with event count; this is separate from peak live memory. Current-state callbacks avoid this history cost. Numerical differentiation repeats it at each likelihood evaluation. Undeclared latent access through ... does not select this sequential path. When mu is an observed-baseline function, the impact's mu argument is the parameter-bound function, as in the R engine. Callbacks must be deterministic and keep captured inputs fixed. Analytic gradients support current-component feedback with the derivatives below; full intensity histories require numerical differentiation.

For an observed baseline with gradient = "analytic", supply jacobian$mu as a matrix or function receiving the observed context. Its param is the full named optimization vector. Return a dimensions-by-parameters matrix with a column for every fitted parameter, including zero columns. Include dependencies through resolved alpha and beta. The baseline value function keeps its local parameter vector. The baseline Jacobian at n = 1 also enters the derivative of automatic initialization. Declare needed N and Nc in the value function or supply their paths.

An analytic impact that explicitly declares lambda_component_n requires jacobian$impact = list(param = ..., state = ...). Each entry is a constant matrix or function receiving the same observed and current-component context. The Jacobians' param is the full named optimization vector. The param matrix has one row per impact entry and one named column per fitted parameter; differentiate the impact while holding lambda_component_n fixed, including direct dependencies through core components. The state matrix is square, with rows for impact entries and columns for current-component entries, both in as.vector() column-major order. It contains the partial derivative of the impact with respect to that pre-jump state. The package propagates state sensitivities through decay, event jumps, and initial components. Do not add those propagated effects again to the supplied param Jacobian. All Jacobians must be finite numeric matrices of constant dimensions. Derivatives must exist along the evaluated parameter path. Branches based only on observations are allowed; parameter-dependent discontinuities and arbitrary reads of lambda or lambda_component are unsupported. Current-state sensitivity storage grows with kernel components times fitted parameters. An observed baseline Jacobian path also grows with observations times dimensions times parameters. No derivative history of all kernel states is stored. Jacobians are evaluated only when a gradient is requested.

The default uses numerical differentiation and does not run additional curvature checks. With final_hessian = "stable", final curvature is checked after optimization without changing coefficients, log-likelihood, the stored optimizer gradient, return code, or iteration count. The stabilization selects difference steps and checks their consistency. If default numerical Hawkes standard errors contain NaN, a short message suggests this option.

The requested stabilization compares information, inverse information, and standard errors across difference steps. Failed checks, singular or indefinite information, and equality or nearby inequality constraints yield NA covariance for free parameters. Fixed parameters retain zero covariance. Supplied Hessians are retained and checked for invertible positive information. No ridge or eigenvalue clipping is applied. Use fit_diagnostics() to inspect the reason. A numerically stable Hessian does not establish identifiability, stationarity, a global maximum, or correct confidence-interval coverage. Weak excitation, nearby kernel decay rates, short samples, boundary estimates, and nonsmooth callbacks can make Wald inference unreliable. Consider profile likelihood and a bootstrap that preserves the observation design and initial state.

fitted_hspec() uses the saved parameter map to restore the estimated model. fit_initial_state() retrieves the observation window's initial-state arguments. These are suitable for re-evaluating the likelihood and starting a new simulation. Keep observations separately and supply them again for inference. The stored optimization objective can retain data in its function environment. Save the fit with saveRDS() to retain its model, parameter map, and initial-state information.

See also

fit_diagnostics(), fitted_hspec(), fit_initial_state(), logLik(), hspec-class, hsim,hspec-method

Examples


# example 1
mu <- c(0.1, 0.1)
alpha <- matrix(c(0.2, 0.1, 0.1, 0.2), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
beta <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
h <- new("hspec", mu=mu, alpha=alpha, beta=beta)
res <- hsim(h, size=100)
#> Initial intensity components: auto -> mean (unconditional component means).
fit <- hfit(h, inter_arrival = res$inter_arrival, type = res$type)
#> Initial intensity components: auto -> mean (unconditional component means).
#> hfit: equal starting values within each matrix share a parameter (reduced = TRUE; mu, alpha, beta).
#> Use reduced = FALSE to estimate matrix entries separately.
summary(fit)
#> --------------------------------------------
#> Maximum Likelihood estimation
#> BFGS maximization, 29 iterations
#> Return code 0: successful convergence 
#> Log-Likelihood: -245.0405 
#> 4  free parameters
#> Estimates:
#>          Estimate Std. error t value  Pr(> t)    
#> mu1       0.10357    0.01918   5.400 6.67e-08 ***
#> alpha1.1  0.21600    0.09858   2.191  0.02845 *  
#> alpha1.2  0.29650    0.11754   2.523  0.01165 *  
#> beta1.1   1.11245    0.34199   3.253  0.00114 ** 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> --------------------------------------------
# Optional Rcpp gradient for this numeric specification:
# hfit(h, res$inter_arrival, res$type, gradient = "analytic")
fit_diagnostics(fit)$status
#> [1] "not_checked"
estimated <- fitted_hspec(fit)
initial <- fit_initial_state(fit)
inferred <- do.call(logLik, c(list(object = estimated,
  inter_arrival = res$inter_arrival, type = res$type, infer = TRUE), initial))
#> Initial intensity components: mean (unconditional component means).
c(fitted = as.numeric(logLik(fit)), restored = inferred$loglikelihood)
#>    fitted  restored 
#> -245.0405 -245.0405 


# A parameter-only function can keep selected entries fixed at zero.
alpha_fun <- function(param = c(a = 0.2, b = 0.1)) {
  matrix(c(param["a"], 0, param["b"], param["a"]), 2)
}
alpha_jac <- cbind(a = c(1, 0, 0, 1), b = c(0, 0, 1, 0))
h_fun <- new("hspec", mu = mu, alpha = alpha_fun, beta = beta)
# hfit(h_fun, res$inter_arrival, res$type, gradient = "analytic",
#      jacobian = list(alpha = alpha_jac))

# Default auto selects C++ with numerical differentiation; no Jacobian:
# fit_fun <- hfit(h_fun, res$inter_arrival, res$type)

# Observed counts can change the excitation after an event.
count_impact <- function(param = c(a = 0.2), n, N, ...) {
  matrix(param["a"] * (1 + 0.2 * (N[n, 1] %% 2)))
}
count_jac <- function(param, n, N, ...) {
  out <- matrix(0, 1, length(param), dimnames = list(NULL, names(param)))
  out[, "a"] <- 1 + 0.2 * (N[n, 1] %% 2)
  out
}
h_count <- new("hspec", mu = 0.3,
  alpha = function(param = numeric(0)) matrix(0), beta = 1.2,
  impact = count_impact)
# hfit(h_count, inter_arrival, gradient = "analytic",
#      jacobian = list(impact = count_jac))
# Or keep numerical differentiation without a Jacobian:
# hfit(h_count, inter_arrival)

# example 2
# \donttest{
mu <- matrix(c(0.08, 0.08, 0.05, 0.05), nrow = 4)
alpha <- function(param = c(alpha11 = 0, alpha12 = 0.4, alpha33 = 0.5, alpha34 = 0.3)){
  matrix(c(param["alpha11"], param["alpha12"], 0, 0,
           param["alpha12"], param["alpha11"], 0, 0,
           0, 0, param["alpha33"], param["alpha34"],
           0, 0, param["alpha34"], param["alpha33"]), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)
}
beta <- matrix(c(rep(0.6, 8), rep(1.2, 8)), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)

impact <- function(param = c(alpha1n=0, alpha1w=0.2, alpha2n=0.001, alpha2w=0.1),
                   n=n, N=N, ...){

  Psi <- matrix(c(0, 0, param['alpha1w'], param['alpha1n'],
                  0, 0, param['alpha1n'], param['alpha1w'],
                  param['alpha2w'], param['alpha2n'], 0, 0,
                  param['alpha2n'], param['alpha2w'], 0, 0), nrow=4, byrow=TRUE)

  ind <- N[,"N1"][n] - N[,"N2"][n] > N[,"N3"][n] - N[,"N4"][n] + 0.5

  km <- matrix(c(!ind, !ind, !ind, !ind,
                 ind, ind, ind, ind,
                 ind, ind, ind, ind,
                 !ind, !ind, !ind, !ind), nrow = 4, byrow = TRUE)

  km * Psi
}
h <- new("hspec",
         mu = mu, alpha = alpha, beta = beta, impact = impact)
hr <- hsim(h, size=100)
#> Initial intensity components: auto -> zero (no supported unconditional mean formula for this model). Supplying lambda_component0 explicitly is recommended for this model.
plot(hr$arrival, hr$N[,'N1'] - hr$N[,'N2'], type='s')
lines(hr$N[,'N3'] - hr$N[,'N4'], type='s', col='red')

fit <- hfit(h, hr$inter_arrival, hr$type)
#> Initial intensity components: auto -> zero (no supported unconditional mean formula for this model). Supplying lambda_component0 explicitly is recommended for this model.
#> hfit: equal starting values within each matrix share a parameter (reduced = TRUE; mu, beta).
#> Use reduced = FALSE to estimate matrix entries separately.
summary(fit)
#> --------------------------------------------
#> Maximum Likelihood estimation
#> BFGS maximization, 93 iterations
#> Return code 0: successful convergence 
#> Log-Likelihood: -161.4402 
#> 12  free parameters
#> Estimates:
#>         Estimate Std. error t value  Pr(> t)    
#> mu1      0.05505    0.08553   0.644   0.5199    
#> mu3      0.13574    0.05728   2.370   0.0178 *  
#> alpha11 -0.08439    0.06304  -1.339   0.1807    
#> alpha12  0.15298    0.09786   1.563   0.1180    
#> alpha33  0.15324    0.09535   1.607   0.1080    
#> alpha34  0.20791    0.09997   2.080   0.0376 *  
#> beta1.1  0.19707    0.11743   1.678   0.0933 .  
#> beta3.1  0.48965    0.06734   7.271 3.56e-13 ***
#> alpha1n  0.10963    0.12084   0.907   0.3643    
#> alpha1w  0.13428    0.08339   1.610   0.1073    
#> alpha2n -1.46464    0.29218  -5.013 5.36e-07 ***
#> alpha2w  1.19704    0.29707   4.030 5.59e-05 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> --------------------------------------------
# }

# example 3
# \donttest{
mu <- c(0.15, 0.15)
alpha <- matrix(c(0.75, 0.6, 0.6, 0.75), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
beta <- matrix(c(2.6, 2.6, 2.6, 2.6), nrow=2, byrow=TRUE)
rmark <- function(param = c(p=0.65), ...){
  rgeom(1, p=param[1]) + 1
}
impact <- function(param = c(eta1=0.2), alpha, n, mark, ...){
  ma <- matrix(rep(mark[n]-1, 4), nrow = 2)
  alpha * ma * matrix( rep(param["eta1"], 4), nrow=2)
}
h1 <- new("hspec", mu=mu, alpha=alpha, beta=beta,
          rmark = rmark,
          impact=impact)
res <- hsim(h1, size=100, lambda_component0 = matrix(rep(0.1,4), nrow=2))

fit <- hfit(h1,
            inter_arrival = res$inter_arrival,
            type = res$type,
            mark = res$mark,
            lambda_component0 = matrix(rep(0.1,4), nrow=2))
#> hfit: equal starting values within each matrix share a parameter (reduced = TRUE; mu, alpha, beta).
#> Use reduced = FALSE to estimate matrix entries separately.
summary(fit)
#> --------------------------------------------
#> Maximum Likelihood estimation
#> BFGS maximization, 37 iterations
#> Return code 0: successful convergence 
#> Log-Likelihood: -191.1433 
#> 5  free parameters
#> Estimates:
#>          Estimate Std. error t value  Pr(> t)    
#> mu1       0.10755    0.02308   4.659 3.17e-06 ***
#> alpha1.1  0.62799    0.23802   2.638  0.00833 ** 
#> alpha1.2  0.55832    0.21164   2.638  0.00834 ** 
#> beta1.1   2.11657    0.67686   3.127  0.00177 ** 
#> eta1      0.10179    0.27794   0.366  0.71418    
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
#> --------------------------------------------
# }
